name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
benefit: A plain patch transformer is easy to resize, distill, and profile module by module.
limitation: Fixed patching is expensive on long pages and can erase small glyphs when the page is resized.

name: CLIP contrastive pretraining
benefit: Provides broadly transferable visual semantics and a simple region-text contrastive objective.
limitation: Web image-text alignment rewards global semantics more than exact character identity or layout.

name: DINO self-distillation
benefit: Learns strong spatial features without text labels and can initialize document regions.
limitation: Teacher centering and multi-crop training are compute-heavy and do not teach transcription.

name: DINOv2 curated self-supervision
benefit: Offers robust dense visual features and a strong non-language vision-transfer control.
limitation: Its natural-image curation and resolution do not target tiny text or document reading order.

name: SigLIP sigmoid contrastive loss
benefit: Avoids global softmax normalization and scales image-text training with simpler pairwise loss.
limitation: Pairwise semantic alignment alone cannot guarantee OCR fidelity or evidence localization.

name: SigLIP 2 multilingual and dense transfer
benefit: Combines multilingual image-text learning with dense and localization-aware visual signals.
limitation: A transferred tower may import natural-image biases and its full variants exceed the vision budget.

name: ConvNeXt V2 fully convolutional masked pretraining
benefit: Supplies a convolutional control with strong locality and favorable deployment kernels.
limitation: A fixed-resolution hierarchy makes arbitrary page geometry and token-level fusion less direct.

name: NaViT native-resolution packing
benefit: Preserves aspect ratio and packs variable-resolution pages without global image distortion.
limitation: Token counts vary sharply for dense pages and require careful batching and positional handling.

name: EVA-02 masked image modeling
benefit: Distills visual semantics into a strong ViT initialization using masked image prediction.
limitation: The teacher targets emphasize visual semantics rather than exact document strings.

name: Segment Anything promptable segmentation
benefit: Can propose regions for pseudo-labeling and region-aware curriculum construction.
limitation: The full model is too large and object masks do not correspond reliably to text evidence units.

name: Flamingo Perceiver Resampler and gated cross-attention
benefit: Compresses variable visual inputs to a fixed latent set and gates visual injection into a frozen LM.
limitation: Repeated cross-attention blocks add parameters and the few-shot design is excessive for a 790M student.

name: BLIP-2 Q-Former
benefit: A compact query transformer bridges frozen vision and language towers with staged alignment.
limitation: A small fixed query set can bottleneck dense pages and learned queries may ignore tiny text.

name: LLaVA linear projector alignment
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison and Microsoft Research
benefit: A minimal projector gives a cheap baseline and cleanly isolates the value of connector complexity.
limitation: Linear alignment offers no explicit compression, ordering, or region selection for long documents.

name: MobileVLM lightweight downsample projector
benefit: Uses local downsampling to reduce visual tokens while preserving neighborhood information.
limitation: Aggressive spatial reduction can cross the OCR legibility cliff on small fonts.

name: MM1 C-Abstractor and data-mixture ablations
benefit: Provides controlled evidence on connector type, image resolution, visual tokens, and data mixture.
limitation: Its reported optima come from larger general-purpose models rather than strict sub-1B documents.

name: PaliGemma prefix-LM multimodal integration
benefit: A simple image-prefix decoder interface supports transfer across detection, captioning, and VQA.
limitation: The released scale and broad task mixture do not resolve the dense-document token bottleneck.

name: Idefics2 image splitting and Perceiver pooling
benefit: Combines high-resolution image splitting with learned token pooling in an open training recipe.
limitation: Tiling increases duplicate context and may separate a label from its value or chart legend.

name: LLaVA-OneVision AnyRes-9
benefit: Adapts grid resolution to image geometry and preserves more high-resolution evidence.
limitation: Multiple tiles inflate LM sequence length and make page-level relationships harder for a small decoder.

name: Perceiver latent bottleneck
benefit: Cross-attention maps very large inputs into a bounded latent array with scalable compute.
limitation: A fixed latent bottleneck can discard rare text evidence unless training explicitly covers it.

name: Qwen2-VL Naive Dynamic Resolution
benefit: Represents images at native aspect ratios and exposes spatial coordinates through multimodal rotary positions.
limitation: Unbounded visual sequences are incompatible with predictable sub-1B latency without a hard token budget.

name: LayoutLM joint text and layout pretraining
benefit: Shows that explicit 2D positions materially help form and receipt understanding.
limitation: It assumes external OCR tokens, creating a pipeline dependency and inherited OCR errors.

name: LayoutLMv3 unified text-image masking
benefit: Unifies masked language, masked image, and word-patch alignment objectives.
limitation: The encoder-only formulation does not directly provide open-ended multilingual generation.

name: DocFormer multimodal self-attention
benefit: Combines text, vision, and spatial features at each layer for strong document representations.
limitation: It depends on OCR tokens and dense multimodal fusion is costly at page scale.

name: Donut OCR-free document parsing
benefit: Demonstrates end-to-end image-to-structure training and introduces scalable synthetic document generation.
limitation: Autoregressive full-page parsing can be slow and weakly grounded without explicit regions.

name: Pix2Struct screenshot parsing pretraining
benefit: Learns visual language from screenshot-to-HTML parsing with variable-resolution inputs.
limitation: HTML reconstruction favors web structure and may waste capacity on markup irrelevant to extraction.

name: UDOP unified document task tokens
benefit: Unifies text, image, and layout generation under task-conditioned objectives.
limitation: Its OCR-assisted inputs and encoder-decoder stack complicate a nearly random decoder-only student.

name: Nougat scientific PDF transcription
benefit: Targets equations, tables, and scientific markup directly from document images.
limitation: Transcription does not by itself teach claim-evidence relations or question answering.

name: UReader low-cost high-resolution adaptation
organization: University of Science and Technology of China
benefit: Adapts frozen low-resolution VLMs to high-resolution documents with shape-adaptive cropping.
limitation: Crop selection can fragment cross-region evidence and relies on a capable frozen base.

name: mPLUG-DocOwl 1.5 structure-aware parsing
benefit: Uses structure-aware parsing and document instruction tuning across varied document tasks.
limitation: Teacher-scale recipes and generated instructions can carry parsing and answer hallucinations.

name: GOT-OCR 2.0 unified OCR
benefit: Unifies plain, formatted, fine-grained, and interactive OCR in a compact generative model.
limitation: OCR specialization provides limited evidence for open-ended relational document reasoning.

name: Florence-2 task-token vision foundation model
benefit: A compact sequence-to-sequence interface covers captioning, detection, grounding, and OCR.
limitation: Task-token specialization lacks a native free-form document reasoning contract.

name: Kosmos-2.5 spatially aware document pretraining
benefit: Combines text-line grounding with markdown-style document generation in one spatially aware objective.
limitation: Line-level coordinates can miss cell, chart-mark, and formula-symbol relationships.

name: SmolDocling document conversion
benefit: Shows that a 256M-scale vision-language model can emit rich document structure.
limitation: Conversion accuracy and reasoning breadth remain capacity-limited on dense or adversarial pages.

name: PaddleOCR-VL dynamic-resolution document parsing
benefit: Pairs a dynamic-resolution encoder with a compact LM for multilingual text, tables, formulas, and charts.
limitation: Its parsing-first objective does not guarantee question-conditioned relational reasoning.

name: TableFormer table structure recognition
benefit: Separates table structure sequence prediction from cell box regression for aligned outputs.
limitation: A specialist table architecture does not naturally share capacity with OCR, charts, and free-form QA.

name: Multi-Query Attention
benefit: Shares key-value heads to reduce autoregressive memory bandwidth and cache size.
limitation: A single KV head may reduce cross-region binding diversity in dense documents.

name: Grouped-Query Attention
benefit: Trades quality and KV-cache cost between multi-head and multi-query attention.
limitation: Conversion from an MHA teacher requires uptraining and may lose specialized heads.

name: Rotary Position Embedding
benefit: Encodes relative position without learned absolute tables and supports length scaling.
limitation: One-dimensional token positions do not encode page geometry unless extended multimodally.

name: RMSNorm
benefit: Removes mean centering for a simpler and efficient normalization layer.
limitation: It does not address activation outliers or multimodal scale mismatch by itself.

name: SwiGLU feed-forward activation
benefit: Gated feed-forward layers improve parameter efficiency over standard ReLU MLPs.
limitation: Three projections increase MLP parameter share and may squeeze the vision budget.

name: FlashAttention exact IO-aware attention
benefit: Reduces attention memory traffic while preserving exact attention outputs.
limitation: Kernel availability is hardware-dependent and does not reduce quadratic arithmetic.

name: FlashAttention-2 work partitioning
benefit: Improves GPU occupancy and parallelism for long visual-language sequences.
limitation: It is not beneficial or available on every deployment GPU; eager remains the reproducible default.

name: Mamba selective state spaces
organization: Carnegie Mellon University and Princeton University
benefit: Provides linear-time sequence modeling with content-dependent state updates.
limitation: Precise retrieval and arbitrary cross-region binding may be weaker than explicit attention.

name: Hyena implicit long convolution
benefit: Models long visual-language sequences with subquadratic implicit convolutional operators and controlled memory.
limitation: Long convolutions offer less interpretable evidence routing and weaker mature inference support.

name: Griffin gated linear recurrences with local attention
benefit: Hybrid recurrent and local-attention blocks reduce long-context cost while retaining local precision.
limitation: The optimal recurrent-to-attention ratio for 2D document evidence is unknown.

name: Knowledge distillation with softened logits
benefit: Transfers teacher class relations through temperature-scaled output distributions.
limitation: Token-level logits can reproduce teacher hallucinations and provide weak spatial supervision.

name: FitNets intermediate representation hints
benefit: Uses intermediate teacher features to train a thinner or deeper student.
limitation: Teacher-student width mismatch needs regressors and layer pairing can be arbitrary.

name: DistilBERT alternating-layer initialization
benefit: Directly copying alternating teacher layers gives a strong, cheap selective-transfer baseline.
limitation: It requires compatible hidden dimensions and can preserve teacher depth-specific biases.

name: TinyBERT two-stage transformer distillation
benefit: Distills embeddings, attention, hidden states, and predictions in general and task-specific stages.
limitation: Matching every signal is memory-intensive and loss scales can conflict in multimodal training.

name: MiniLM attention relation distillation
benefit: Transfers self-attention relations without requiring identical hidden width.
limitation: Language-only attention relations omit visual token selection and spatial alignment.

name: MiniLMv2 multi-head self-attention relation distillation
benefit: Supports flexible teacher-student head and width configurations through relation matrices.
limitation: Quadratic relation targets are costly for long visual sequences.

name: MobileBERT inverted bottleneck transfer
benefit: Uses bottleneck projections and a specially trained teacher to transfer into a narrow model.
limitation: Training a width-compatible teacher adds a substantial preliminary stage.

name: DeiT distillation token
benefit: Adds a dedicated token for teacher supervision in data-efficient vision training.
limitation: A global distillation token cannot convey all page regions or exact text sequences.

name: Distilling Step-by-Step rationale supervision
benefit: Uses teacher rationales as additional supervision for small-model reasoning.
limitation: The repository's measured LFM ablation found free rationale targets harmful at current scale and quality.

name: BERT-of-Theseus progressive module replacement
organization: Peking University and Microsoft Research Asia
benefit: Gradually replaces teacher blocks with fewer student blocks instead of training the compressed model abruptly.
limitation: Joint teacher-student execution raises memory cost and assumes compatible block interfaces.

name: Minitron structured pruning plus distillation
benefit: Derives smaller models by pruning depth, width, attention, and MLP dimensions then retraining with KD.
limitation: A pruned language teacher does not determine the right vision-language budget split.

name: SparseGPT one-shot weight pruning
benefit: Produces high unstructured sparsity with a layerwise second-order approximation.
limitation: Sparse weights may not accelerate commodity inference and pruning can damage rare scripts.

name: Wanda activation-aware pruning
benefit: Ranks weights using magnitude and input activations without retraining or Hessian inversion.
limitation: Calibration data determines what survives, so thin-language or hard-document features can vanish.

name: QLoRA 4-bit adapter training
benefit: Makes teacher adaptation and broad ablations feasible under constrained GPU memory.
limitation: It reduces training memory, not the final dense student architecture or its pretraining cost.

name: LoRA low-rank adaptation
benefit: Supports controlled module-placement experiments with few trainable parameters.
limitation: Adapter gains on a pretrained LFM do not prove that the same capability can be learned from near-random initialization.

name: SynthText scene text rendering
benefit: Renders text into natural images with geometry-aware placement and automatic labels.
limitation: Scene composition does not model document hierarchy, tables, or relational questions.

name: MJSynth synthetic word engine
benefit: Shows large-scale rendered word crops can train recognition without manual labels.
limitation: Isolated words omit page context, reading order, and evidence relations.

name: SynthTIGER multilingual text image generation
benefit: Provides configurable multilingual typography, layouts, and augmentation for OCR training.
limitation: Language coverage still depends on fonts and corpora; generated layouts can be recognizably synthetic.

name: UnrealText 3D scene text synthesis
benefit: Uses 3D environments to create realistic perspective, lighting, and occlusion for text.
limitation: The rendering cost and scene focus add little to digital-native tables and scientific pages.

name: DoReMi domain reweighting
benefit: Learns domain weights using excess loss so weak domains receive more useful training mass.
limitation: Proxy-model weights can be unstable and may chase noisy or intrinsically difficult sources.

name: DataComp controlled multimodal data filtering
benefit: Treats dataset filtering as the controlled variable under a fixed compute budget.
limitation: CLIP-like filtering favors semantic image-caption pairs over precise text and document structure.

name: DataComp-LM data curation benchmark
benefit: Provides reproducible data curation experiments under fixed language-model compute.
limitation: Text-only quality signals do not measure visual grounding or OCR label fidelity.

name: Textbooks Are All You Need synthetic curriculum
benefit: Demonstrates that high-quality, curriculum-like synthetic data can compensate for small model size.
limitation: Generated educational text can be narrow, duplicated, and disconnected from real visual distributions.

name: Self-Instruct bootstrapped instruction generation
benefit: Expands task instructions from a small seed set with filtering and deduplication.
limitation: Text-only generation cannot verify whether an instruction is answerable from document pixels.

name: SVIT scalable visual instruction tuning
benefit: Generates large visual instruction sets including reasoning and region-level tasks.
limitation: Teacher-generated visual answers can hallucinate details absent from the image.

name: ALLaVA low-cost caption and instruction generation
benefit: Uses compact captioning and instruction pipelines to improve data scale and diversity efficiently.
limitation: Synthetic answer quality remains bounded by teacher perception and filtering.

name: ChartQA human and augmented chart questions
benefit: Combines human questions with generated arithmetic questions over chart source data.
limitation: Template augmentation can be solved by shortcuts and covers limited chart grammars.

name: FinQA program-supervised financial reasoning
benefit: Supplies executable reasoning programs over financial reports for verifiable answers.
limitation: Most evidence is textual and the program vocabulary covers only a bounded operation set.

name: TAT-QA hybrid table-text financial reasoning
organization: Nanjing University and Microsoft Research Asia
benefit: Requires arithmetic over both tables and surrounding prose with scale and unit normalization.
limitation: Dataset artifacts and extracted inputs underrepresent raw-page perception failures.

name: SciGraphQA graph-grounded scientific figure QA
benefit: Connects scientific figures, captions, and paper context for graph-grounded questions.
limitation: Automatically generated questions may reward caption matching instead of visual scientific reasoning.

name: InstructGPT PPO with human preferences
benefit: Establishes the SFT, reward-model, and KL-regularized PPO alignment pipeline.
limitation: A learned scalar reward is expensive and vulnerable to visual hallucination and reward misspecification.

name: Direct Preference Optimization
benefit: Optimizes preferences without an explicit reward model or online policy rollouts.
limitation: Requires reliable chosen-rejected pairs and does not exploit exact document rewards directly.

name: Identity Preference Optimization
benefit: Provides a regularized preference objective with a direct theoretical target.
limitation: Offline pair quality still dominates and multimodal grounding errors may be invisible to preferences.

name: Kahneman-Tversky Optimization
benefit: Learns from binary desirable or undesirable outputs without paired preferences.
limitation: Binary labels discard how much a box, table, or numeric answer is wrong.

name: Odds Ratio Preference Optimization
benefit: Combines supervised likelihood with an odds-ratio preference term in one stage.
limitation: Token likelihood can dominate structured document correctness and preference calibration.

name: Simple Preference Optimization
benefit: Uses a reference-free margin objective with length normalization.
limitation: Length normalization does not solve wrong evidence or visually ungrounded rationales.

name: REINFORCE Leave-One-Out
benefit: Offers a simple online RL baseline without a learned value model.
limitation: Multiple sampled sequences remain expensive for long structured outputs.

name: Group Relative Policy Optimization
benefit: Uses group-relative rewards without a critic, fitting verifiable document objectives.
limitation: Group sampling multiplies decoding cost and weak reward variance can destabilize a small policy.

name: Constitutional AI
benefit: Uses explicit principles and AI feedback to scale behavioral supervision.
limitation: A constitution cannot objectively judge OCR strings, boxes, formulas, or financial arithmetic.

name: RL from AI Feedback
benefit: Substitutes scalable AI preferences for expensive human comparisons.
limitation: An AI judge may share the policy's visual blind spots and reward fluent unsupported answers.

name: Self-Rewarding Language Models
organization: Meta AI and New York University
benefit: Improves both instruction following and internal judging through iterative preference training.
limitation: A sub-1B policy is unlikely to be a trustworthy judge of its own hard document reasoning.

name: Reinforced Self-Training
benefit: Alternates generation, reward filtering, and fine-tuning without continuous online RL.
limitation: Filtering can collapse diversity and amplify reward-model shortcuts.

name: Self-Play Fine-Tuning
benefit: Uses the model's previous policy to create negative responses without a stronger external teacher.
limitation: Self-play cannot introduce visual facts the model never perceived and may reinforce existing errors.

name: RLAIF-V open-source multimodal feedback
benefit: Targets multimodal helpfulness and hallucination using AI-generated preference feedback.
limitation: Preference judges are less reliable than authored ground truth for exact document tasks.

name: Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
benefit: Applies GRPO with task-specific verifiable visual rewards such as IoU.
limitation: Reported gains use larger VLMs and narrow perception tasks; long document outputs raise rollout cost.

name: Focal Loss
benefit: Downweights easy examples so rare and hard visual elements receive more gradient.
limitation: Hard synthetic noise can dominate unless difficulty and label quality are separated.

name: Generalized IoU loss
benefit: Provides box learning signal even when predicted and target boxes do not overlap.
limitation: One box score does not encode reading order, evidence identity, or nested regions.

name: Distance-IoU and Complete-IoU losses
benefit: Adds center distance and aspect-ratio terms for faster and more precise box regression.
limitation: Aspect penalties can be unstable for lines, cells, and extremely thin document regions.

name: Supervised Contrastive Learning
benefit: Clusters same-label features while separating hard negatives, useful for region-text alignment.
limitation: False negatives occur when repeated values or visually similar glyphs have different semantics.

name: Temperature scaling for calibration
benefit: Adds a cheap post-hoc calibration baseline without changing predictions.
limitation: Sequence confidence and distribution shift are not corrected by one global temperature.

name: Deep ensembles
benefit: Offers a strong uncertainty baseline and detects disagreement on ambiguous documents.
limitation: Multiple sub-1B models violate the intended deployment latency and memory budget.

name: Conformal risk control
benefit: Provides finite-sample control of deployment risk under explicit assumptions.
limitation: Coverage guarantees weaken under domain shift and require a representative calibration set.

name: SelectiveNet integrated abstention
benefit: Learns prediction and coverage jointly so the model can abstain on unreliable inputs.
limitation: Coverage objectives can reject entire difficult languages instead of improving them.

name: PCGrad conflicting-gradient projection
benefit: Projects conflicting task gradients to reduce destructive interference in multitask training.
limitation: Pairwise gradient operations add cost and may hide a fundamentally poor data mixture.

name: GradNorm adaptive task loss balancing
benefit: Balances task losses using relative training rates instead of fixed hand-tuned weights.
limitation: Loss-rate balance does not guarantee equal downstream value or protect rare language slices.
